findings.message: mktemp creates a world-accessible path in /tmp; a local attacker who replaces the file between the subshell write (printf '$?' > ...) and the parent-shell read (cat) could substitute an arbitrary integer, causing the wrong disposition word to be emitted — at worst 'complete' instead of 'timed_out', which re-introduces the false-convergence defect this change exists to prevent.

Same mktemp-in-/tmp pattern as spec-coverage: a local attacker could overwrite the rc file between the inner-subshell write and the outer read, controlling which disposition word is written to spec-correspondence-result.json.
